big_ideas.title: Equilibrium is an extremum under constraints
big_ideas.text: An isolated system maximises its entropy; a system coupled to a bath minimises the matching free energy. Every equilibrium condition — equal T, P, μ; K; coexistence — is that extremum written out.

big_ideas.title: One fundamental equation holds everything
big_ideas.text: S(U,V,N) or U(S,V,N) contains all equilibrium information; F, H, G and Ω are the same information re-expressed in the variables a lab controls, by Legendre transform.

big_ideas.title: Calculus turns the unmeasurable into the measurable
big_ideas.text: Maxwell relations and derivative identities rewrite entropy and chemical-potential changes in terms of P–V–T data, heat capacities, α and κ_T.

big_ideas.title: Stability is curvature
big_ideas.text: Concave entropy (convex energy) means positive heat capacities and compressibilities; where curvature fails, a single phase splits and phase transitions, spinodals and critical points appear.

big_ideas.title: Chemical potential moves matter
big_ideas.text: Matter flows from high to low μ between phases, across membranes, into solution and through reactions; nonideality enters only through fugacity and activity.

big_ideas.title: Macroscopic properties are Boltzmann-weighted averages
big_ideas.text: Count microstates, weight them by e^(−βE), sum into a partition function; its logarithm is a free energy, its derivatives are U, S, P, μ, and its second derivatives are fluctuations.

practices.title: Define the system and constraints
practices.text: Say what is isolated, what exchanges energy, volume or particles with a bath, and which variables are held fixed.

practices.title: Pick the potential or ensemble
practices.text: Match the controlled variables to the potential that is extremised (S, F, G, Ω) and to the ensemble (microcanonical, canonical, grand, isobaric).

practices.title: Manipulate derivatives
practices.text: Use exact differentials, Legendre transforms, Maxwell relations, the triple-product and chain rules to reach a derivative you can evaluate.

practices.title: Build a molecular model
practices.text: Count states, choose a lattice, two-level, oscillator, rotor or ideal-gas model, and assemble the partition function from independent pieces.

practices.title: Compute with units
practices.text: R vs k_B, per mole vs per molecule, kelvin, wavenumbers to energy, standard states for K, fugacity and activity.

practices.title: Check and reason
practices.text: Signs, limiting cases (T → 0, T → ∞, ideal limit, large N), stability, and which way a change pushes equilibrium.

los.do: Count ordered selections of distinguishable objects (permutations).
ek: N!/(N − k)! ordered ways to fill k slots from N.

los.do: Count arrangements of indistinguishable particles on distinguishable sites.
ek: C(M, N) = M!/(N!(M − N)!) — the lattice-gas multiplicity.

los.do: Count distinct sequences of a multiset (multinomial coefficient).
ek: N!/(n_A! n_B! …); identical units are not reordered.

los.do: Apply Stirling's approximation to ln W for large N.
ek: ln N! ≈ N ln N − N; turns ln C(M, N) into −M Σ x ln x.

los.do: Calculate the probability of exactly k outcomes in N independent two-outcome trials.
Calculate an 'at least one' probability through the complement.
ek: P(≥ 1) = 1 − (1 − p)^N for independent events.

los.do: Calculate the mean and variance of a discrete distribution.
ek: ⟨x⟩ = Σ p_i x_i; σ² = ⟨x²⟩ − ⟨x⟩².

units.title: Entropy, equilibrium and the fundamental equation

topics.title: Multiplicity and S = k ln W

los.do: Calculate the multiplicity of a system of independent two-state units with a given number excited.
ek: W = N!/(n!(N − n)!); S = k_B ln W.

los.do: Calculate the multiplicity of an Einstein solid with N oscillators and q quanta.
Calculate ΔS from the change in multiplicity of a lattice or spin system.
ek: ΔS = k_B ln(W₂/W₁).

los.do: Derive the entropy of isothermal ideal-gas expansion by lattice counting.
ek: W ∝ M^N, M ∝ V ⇒ ΔS = nR ln(V₂/V₁).

los.do: Calculate the probability of each energy split between two solids in thermal contact and identify the most probable one.
ek: P(q_A) ∝ W_A(q_A) W_B(q − q_A); the peak sharpens as N grows.

los.do: Derive equality of T, P and μ by maximising total entropy over exchange of U, V and N.
ek: ∂S/∂U = 1/T, ∂S/∂V = P/T, ∂S/∂N = −μ/T must match across the wall.

los.do: Show that maximum entropy at fixed U is equivalent to minimum energy at fixed S.
ek: Internal constraints released ⇒ S rises (second law); the energy-minimum principle is its inverse.

topics.title: The fundamental equation and its integrated forms

los.do: Find T, P or μ as derivatives of a given S(U, V, N).
ek: dS = (1/T)dU + (P/T)dV − (μ/T)dN.

los.do: Find T, P or μ as derivatives of a given U(S, V, N).
ek: dU = T dS − P dV + μ dN.

los.do: Check that a proposed fundamental equation is extensive (first-order homogeneous).
ek: S(λU, λV, λN) = λS(U, V, N); exponents of extensive variables sum to 1.

los.do: Calculate U, or any one term, from the Euler relation.
ek: U = TS − PV + μN; equivalently G = μN for one component.

los.do: Apply the Gibbs–Duhem equation to relate changes in the intensive variables.
ek: S dT − V dP + N dμ = 0; at fixed T, dμ = v dP.

topics.title: Work and heat on reversible paths

los.do: Calculate q, w and ΔU for a reversible isothermal ideal-gas process.
ek: ΔU = 0; w = −nRT ln(V₂/V₁) = −q.

los.do: Calculate q, w and ΔU for a reversible isobaric ideal-gas process.
ek: w = −PΔV = −nRΔT; q = nC_pΔT.

los.do: Calculate q, w and ΔU for a constant-volume ideal-gas process.
ek: w = 0; q = ΔU = nC_vΔT.

los.do: Find the final state of a reversible adiabatic ideal-gas process.
ek: TV^(γ−1) constant; C_v = 3R/2 monatomic, 5R/2 diatomic (no vibration).

los.do: Calculate the total entropy change of system plus bath for an irreversible process and decide whether it can occur.
ek: ΔS_bath = −q/T_bath; ΔS_tot ≥ 0, equal only when reversible.

los.do: Calculate the maximum efficiency or coefficient of performance of a cycle between two reservoirs.
ek: η_max = 1 − T_C/T_H from ΔS_tot = 0.

los.do: Apply steady-flow energy and entropy balances to a turbine, compressor, nozzle or throttle.
ek: Δh = q + w_s per unit mass; throttling is isenthalpic; Δs ≥ q/T.

los.do: Test whether a differential is exact (a state function) by equality of cross-derivatives.
ek: M dx + N dy exact ⇔ ∂M/∂y = ∂N/∂x; δq and δw are not exact.

los.do: Apply the triple-product and chain rules to rewrite a partial derivative.
Construct F, H or G from a given U(S, V, N) by Legendre transform.
ek: F = U − TS; eliminate S using T = ∂U/∂S. H = U + PV; G = U − TS + PV.

los.do: State the natural variables and differential of any potential, including the grand potential.
ek: dF = −S dT − P dV + μ dN; dG = −S dT + V dP + μ dN; dΩ = −S dT − P dV − N dμ.

los.do: Choose the potential minimised at equilibrium for given bath conditions.
ek: T, V, N → F; T, P, N → G; T, V, μ → Ω; S, P, N → H.

los.do: Derive P, S, μ or U from a given F(T, V, N) or G(T, P, N).
Use the Gibbs–Helmholtz relation to get S or H from G(T).
Identify the Maxwell relation that equals a given partial derivative.
ek: Cross-derivatives of the potential whose natural variables are the two held fixed: (∂S/∂V)_T = (∂P/∂T)_V from F.

los.do: Evaluate an entropy derivative from an equation of state through a Maxwell relation.
Express a thermodynamic derivative in terms of α, κ_T and c_p and evaluate it.
Estimate the pressure rise when a liquid is heated at constant volume.
ek: ΔP ≈ (α/κ_T) ΔT — large for liquids (tens of bar per K).

los.do: Derive and evaluate c_p − c_v from α and κ_T.
ek: c_p − c_v = Tvα²/κ_T; = R for an ideal gas.

los.do: Derive (∂U/∂V)_T or the Joule–Thomson coefficient for a real gas from its equation of state.
Decide whether a fundamental equation is stable from the concavity of S(U, V).
ek: ∂²S/∂U² ≤ 0, ∂²S/∂V² ≤ 0, and the Hessian determinant ≥ 0.

los.do: Derive C_V from a fundamental equation and check that it is positive.
ek: C_V = (∂U/∂T)_V = −(∂S/∂U)²/(∂²S/∂U²) > 0 for stability.

los.do: Test whether a homogeneous van der Waals state is mechanically stable.
ek: Stable ⇔ (∂P/∂V)_T < 0 ⇔ κ_T > 0.

los.do: Calculate κ_T of a fluid from its equation of state.
ek: κ_T = −1/[V(∂P/∂V)_T]; for vdW (∂P/∂V)_T = −RT/(V − b)² + 2a/V³.

los.do: Find the critical constants of a cubic equation of state.
ek: (∂P/∂V)_T = (∂²P/∂V²)_T = 0; vdW: T_c = 8a/27Rb, V_c = 3b, P_c = a/27b².

los.do: Locate the spinodal and classify a state as stable, metastable or unstable.
ek: Spinodal: (∂P/∂V)_T = 0; between binodal and spinodal the state is metastable.

los.do: Find coexisting states by a common tangent on G or F, or Maxwell's equal-area rule on a vdW isotherm.
ek: Equal μ and P in both phases ⇔ common tangent ⇔ ∫P dV over the loop = P_sat ΔV.

los.do: Write μ(T, P) for a pure ideal gas and for a component of an ideal-gas mixture and calculate Δμ.
ek: μ = μ°(T) + RT ln(P/P°); in a mixture replace P by p_i = y_iP.

los.do: Calculate Z and residual (departure) properties from a virial or cubic equation of state.
ek: Z = PV/RT = 1 + B/V + …; h − h^ig = ∫[T(∂P/∂T)_V − P]dV + RT(Z − 1).

los.do: Calculate a fugacity coefficient from a virial or cubic equation of state.
ek: ln φ = ∫₀^P (Z − 1) dP/P; truncated virial: ln φ = BP/RT.

los.do: Relate the second virial coefficient to the intermolecular pair potential.
ek: B(T) = −2πN_A ∫(e^(−βu(r)) − 1) r² dr; B < 0 when attraction dominates.

los.do: Estimate properties of a gas or gas mixture by corresponding states and mixing rules.
ek: Z = f(T_r, P_r, ω); a_mix = ΣΣ y_iy_j √(a_ia_j)(1 − k_ij), b_mix = Σ y_ib_i.

topics.title: Conditions for phase equilibrium and the phase rule

los.do: State the conditions for phase coexistence and apply the Gibbs phase rule to a phase diagram.
ek: T, P, μ_i equal in every phase; F = C − π + 2.

los.do: Calculate the slope of a coexistence curve from the Clapeyron equation.
ek: dP/dT = Δh/(TΔv).

los.do: Estimate a vapor pressure at a new temperature with the integrated Clausius–Clapeyron equation.
ek: ln(P₂/P₁) = −(Δh_vap/R)(1/T₂ − 1/T₁); ideal vapor, v_liq ≪ v_vap, constant Δh.

los.do: Find Δh_vap from vapor pressures at two temperatures.
ek: Slope of ln P vs 1/T is −Δh_vap/R.

los.do: Find the boiling temperature at a new pressure.
ek: 1/T₂ = 1/T₁ − (R/Δh_vap) ln(P₂/P₁).

topics.title: Order parameters and types of transition

los.do: Classify a transition as first- or second-order from which derivatives of G are discontinuous.
ek: First order: jumps in S, V (latent heat); continuous: jumps or divergences in C_p, κ_T; the order parameter vanishes at T_c.

los.do: Calculate the entropy of ideal mixing.
ek: ΔS_mix = −nR Σ x_i ln x_i (from lattice counting).

los.do: Calculate the Gibbs energy of ideal mixing.
ek: ΔG_mix = nRT Σ x_i ln x_i; ΔH_mix = ΔV_mix = 0.

topics.title: Partial molar quantities and Gibbs–Duhem in mixtures

los.do: Calculate partial molar properties from a total property, e.g. by the tangent-intercept method.
ek: v̄_i = (∂V/∂n_i)_{T,P,n_j}; V = Σ n_i v̄_i.

los.do: Use Gibbs–Duhem to get one activity coefficient from the other or to test data for consistency.
ek: Σ x_i d ln γ_i = 0 at fixed T, P.

los.do: Calculate total pressure and vapor composition of an ideal solution with Raoult's law.
ek: p_i = x_iP_i*; P = Σ x_iP_i*; y_i = p_i/P.

los.do: Calculate the solubility of a dilute solute from Henry's law.
ek: p_i = x_iK_H,i for x_i → 0; K_H grows with T for most gases in water.

los.do: Perform bubble-point, dew-point and isothermal flash calculations for a multicomponent mixture.
ek: K_i = y_i/x_i; flash: Σ z_i(K_i − 1)/[1 + β(K_i − 1)] = 0 (Rachford–Rice).

los.do: Calculate activity coefficients from an excess-Gibbs-energy model (regular solution, Margules).
ek: G^ex/n = W x_Ax_B ⇒ RT ln γ_A = W x_B².

los.do: Derive the regular-solution model from a lattice with nearest-neighbour interactions and predict when the mixture phase-separates.
ek: ΔG_mix/nRT = Σ x ln x + χ x_Ax_B; unstable for χ > 2 (upper critical point at χ = 2, x = ½).

los.do: Calculate VLE with modified Raoult's law and identify an azeotrope.
ek: y_iP = x_iγ_iP_i*; at an azeotrope x_i = y_i and γ_A P_A* = γ_B P_B*.

los.do: Calculate boiling-point elevation, freezing-point depression or osmotic pressure of a dilute solution.
ek: ΔT_b = RT_b²x_B/Δh_vap; ΔT_f = RT_f²x_B/Δh_fus; Π = c_BRT (van 't Hoff).

los.do: Relate a partition coefficient to the free energy of transferring a solute between phases.
ek: ΔG°_transfer = −RT ln K_partition; set by μ° differences in the two solvents.

los.do: Calculate K from ΔG°.
ek: K = exp(−ΔG°/RT); standard state fixes the units of each activity.

los.do: Calculate ΔG° from K.
ek: ΔG° = −RT ln K.

los.do: Predict the direction of reaction from Q versus K.
ek: ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q = RT ln(Q/K); Q < K ⇒ forward.

los.do: Solve for the equilibrium extent of reaction and composition from K and the feed.
ek: n_i = n_i0 + ν_iξ; K = Π(y_iP/P°)^ν_i for ideal gases.

los.do: Predict how pressure, inerts or a nonideal phase shift an equilibrium.
ek: K_y = K(P/P°)^(−Δν); raising P favours fewer gas moles; fugacity or activity replaces y_iP in real phases.

los.do: Find ΔH° from K at two temperatures, or K at a new temperature, with the van 't Hoff equation.
ek: d ln K/d(1/T) = −ΔH°/R.

topics.title: Reaction equilibrium from molecular partition functions

los.do: Calculate K for a gas-phase reaction from molecular partition functions.
ek: K = Π(q_i/V)^ν_i e^(−ΔE₀/k_BT) (per standard volume); dissociation energies set ΔE₀.

units.title: The Boltzmann distribution and the canonical ensemble

los.do: Calculate the population ratio of two levels at a given temperature.
ek: N₂/N₁ = (g₂/g₁) e^(−ΔE/k_BT); 1 cm⁻¹ ↔ 1.439 K.

los.do: Calculate the fraction of molecules in a given level of a multi-level system.
ek: p_j = g_j e^(−βE_j)/q.

los.do: Find the temperature at which a level reaches a given population ratio.
ek: T = ΔE/[k_B ln(g₂N₁/g₁N₂)].

topics.title: The partition function and thermodynamic properties

los.do: Calculate a molecular partition function from a list of levels and degeneracies.
ek: q = Σ g_j e^(−βE_j); q counts thermally accessible states.

los.do: Derive the average energy U from ln q for a two-level system or harmonic oscillator.
ek: U = −N ∂ln q/∂β; oscillator U/Nε = 1/(e^x − 1).

los.do: Derive the entropy from the partition function.
ek: S = U/T + Nk_B ln q (localized); S/Nk_B = ln q + βU/N.

los.do: Calculate the Helmholtz free energy from the partition function.
ek: F = −k_BT ln Q; localized independent molecules: Q = q^N.

los.do: Assemble the system partition function from molecular ones for distinguishable or indistinguishable particles.
ek: Q = q^N (localized) or q^N/N! (gas); independent modes multiply: q = q_t q_r q_v q_e.

units.title: Molecular models of gases and solids

topics.title: Translation and the classical ideal gas

los.do: Calculate the thermal de Broglie wavelength of a molecule.
ek: Λ = h/√(2πmk_BT); classical when Λ³ ≪ V/N.

los.do: Calculate the translational partition function of a molecule in a box.
ek: q_trans = V/Λ³.

los.do: Derive the ideal-gas law and the Sackur–Tetrode entropy from Q = q^N/N!.
ek: P = k_BT ∂ln Q/∂V = Nk_BT/V; S/Nk_B = ln(V/NΛ³) + 5/2.

los.do: Calculate the rotational temperature of a diatomic from masses and bond length.
ek: I = μr²; θ_rot = ħ²/(2Ik_B).

los.do: Calculate the high-temperature rotational partition function, including the symmetry number.
ek: q_rot = T/(σθ_rot); σ = 2 homonuclear, 1 heteronuclear.

los.do: Calculate the vibrational temperature and vibrational partition function.
ek: θ_vib = hcν̃/k_B; q_vib = 1/(1 − e^(−θ_vib/T)) from the ground state.

los.do: Calculate the classical heat capacity of a gas by equipartition.
ek: ½k_B per quadratic term: 3 translational, 2 or 3 rotational, 2 per vibration (3N − 5 or 3N − 6 modes).

los.do: Calculate C_V of a diatomic gas with classical translation and rotation and quantum vibration.
ek: C_V,m = 5R/2 + R x²eˣ/(eˣ − 1)², x = θ_vib/T.

los.do: Derive the heat capacity of a two-level (Schottky) system.
ek: C_V = (∂U/∂T)_V; peaks near k_BT ~ ε and vanishes at both limits.

los.do: Derive the heat capacity of a quantum harmonic oscillator.
ek: C_V/Nk_B = x²eˣ/(eˣ − 1)² → 1 classically.

los.do: Calculate the molar heat capacity of a crystal from the Einstein model.
ek: C_V,m = 3R x²eˣ/(eˣ − 1)², x = θ_E/T; Dulong–Petit 3R at high T.

los.do: Apply the Debye T³ law at low temperature and explain why Einstein fails there.
ek: C_V ∝ (T/θ_D)³ at T ≪ θ_D: low-frequency acoustic modes stay active.

los.do: Compute averages from the Maxwell–Boltzmann speed distribution.
ek: f(v) ∝ v² e^(−mv²/2k_BT); v_mp = √(2k_BT/m), ⟨v⟩ = √(8k_BT/πm), v_rms = √(3k_BT/m).

los.do: Write the classical canonical partition function as a phase-space integral and reduce it to a configurational integral.
Calculate an absolute entropy from heat-capacity data, including residual entropy of a disordered crystal.
ek: S(T) = ∫₀^T C_p/T dT + Σ Δh_trans/T_trans; residual S = R ln W per mole (CO: R ln 2).

topics.title: Energy fluctuations in the canonical ensemble

los.do: Calculate the energy variance of a molecule with a few discrete levels.
ek: σ_E² = ⟨E²⟩ − ⟨E⟩² = ∂²ln q/∂β².

los.do: Derive the energy variance of a quantum harmonic oscillator.
ek: σ_E²/ε² = eˣ/(eˣ − 1)².

los.do: Calculate the rms energy fluctuation from the heat capacity.
ek: σ_E² = k_BT²C_V — positive C_V is the stability condition again.

los.do: Calculate the relative energy fluctuation of a macroscopic system and explain why ensembles agree.
ek: σ_E/⟨E⟩ ∝ N^(−1/2); monatomic ideal gas: √(2/3N).

los.do: Calculate the occupancy probabilities of a site exchanging molecules with a reservoir at fixed μ.
ek: Ξ_site = 1 + e^(β(μ + ε)); p_empty = 1/Ξ.

los.do: Calculate the average number of bound molecules on independent sites from the grand partition function.
ek: Ξ = (1 + λe^(βε))^M; ⟨N⟩ = λ ∂ln Ξ/∂λ.

los.do: Calculate the particle-number variance in the grand canonical ensemble.
Calculate the population ratio of two states that differ in energy and volume at fixed T and P.
ek: P_B/P_A = e^(−β(ΔE + PΔV)); G = −k_BT ln Δ.

topics.title: The Gibbs entropy and choosing an ensemble

los.do: Calculate entropy from microstate probabilities with the Gibbs formula and match each ensemble to its potential.
ek: S = −k_B Σ p_i ln p_i; NVE ↔ S, NVT ↔ F, NPT ↔ G, μVT ↔ Ω = −PV.

los.do: Calculate fractional occupancy of a single-site receptor from K_d.
ek: θ = c/(K_d + c).

los.do: Find the gas pressure that gives a target Langmuir coverage.
Calculate the standard binding free energy from K_d.
ek: ΔG°_bind = RT ln(K_d/c°), c° = 1 M.

los.do: Calculate the average number bound to a two-site molecule with a pair interaction from its binding polynomial.
ek: Ξ = 1 + 2y + wy²; ⟨N⟩ = (2y + 2wy²)/Ξ; w > 1 cooperative.

los.do: Calculate fractional saturation from the Hill equation.
Find the Hill coefficient from saturation at two concentrations.
ek: n_H = Δ ln[θ/(1 − θ)] / Δ ln c.

los.do: Solve the Zimm–Bragg helix–coil or 1-D Ising model with a transfer matrix, or a mean-field Ising model for T_c.
ek: Q = λ₁^N for large N; mean field: k_BT_c = zJ.

los.do: Find the activation energy from rate constants at two temperatures.
ek: ln(k₂/k₁) = −(E_a/R)(1/T₂ − 1/T₁).

los.do: Find a rate constant at a new temperature from E_a.
ek: k₂ = k₁ exp[−(E_a/R)(1/T₂ − 1/T₁)].

los.do: Calculate the factor by which a rate rises over a temperature interval.
ek: k₂/k₁ = exp[(E_a/R)(1/T₁ − 1/T₂)]; the 'doubles per 10 K' rule ↔ E_a ≈ 50 kJ/mol near 300 K.

los.do: Calculate a rate constant from ΔH‡ and ΔS‡ with the Eyring equation.
ek: k = (k_BT/h) e^(ΔS‡/R) e^(−ΔH‡/RT).

los.do: Find the activation free energy from a measured rate constant.
ek: ΔG‡ = −RT ln(kh/k_BT).

los.do: Relate forward and reverse rate constants to K by detailed balance and read rates off a free-energy profile along a reaction coordinate.
ek: k_f/k_r = K; barrier height on F(ξ) sets k; catalysts lower ΔG‡, not ΔG°.

los.do: Calculate an equilibrium potential with the Nernst equation and a mean ionic activity coefficient with Debye–Hückel.
ek: E = E° − (RT/zF) ln Q; ln γ± = −A|z₊z₋|√I (dilute limit).

los.do: Calculate the Flory–Huggins free energy of mixing and the critical χ for a polymer solution.
ek: ΔG_mix/k_BT = (φ/N) ln φ + (1 − φ) ln(1 − φ) + χφ(1 − φ); χ_c = ½(1 + 1/√N)².

los.do: Apply the Metropolis acceptance rule and compute an ensemble average from a sampled trajectory.
ek: acc = min(1, e^(−βΔE)); ⟨A⟩ = time average over equilibrated, decorrelated samples.
